cards.title: Scaffold QR Code Forge: Electron + Vite + TypeScript
cards.description: package.json; electron/ main.ts + preload.ts with contextIsolation & IPC bridge; src/ Vite renderer; electron-builder.yml; dev scripts (dev/build/win/linux). FINALIZED: app name "QR Code Forge", productName + app-id io.github.<user>.qrcodeforge (GitHub handle pending, placeholder until then); MIT LICENSE file from day one; all UI strings centralized in src/i18n/en.json so new languages drop in later.
cards.rationale: Foundation card of the 11-card plan decided with the user (scratch over forking the dead Pascal/GPL original). Everything else builds on it.
cards.rejected: Forking Ircama/qr-code-generator; Tauri 2; PySide6; Flathub publication (GitHub Releases + local Flatpak chosen).
cards.summary: Electron 33 + Vite 5 + TS scaffold complete: package.json (QR Code Forge 1.0.0, MIT, io.github.lakisan1.qrcodeforge), electron/main.ts+preload.ts (contextIsolation, sandboxed renderer, minimal IPC: export:save / clipboard:image / app:info), src/ renderer, electron-builder.yml, vite.config.ts, tsconfigs, i18n string table (en), LICENSE. Verified: typecheck ✓ 12 tests ✓ builds ✓ xvfb smoke-test ✓ (window renders, typed URL → live QR).

cards.title: Core generation UI: type selector + content input + live preview
cards.description: Content editor (plain text/URL) with tabbed type selector delegating to the structured content types card; live debounced preview; module size, quiet-zone margin, error-correction level (L/M/Q/H).
cards.rationale: MVP heart of the app; all other features hang off this preview loop.
cards.summary: Tabbed type selector (Text/URL, WiFi, Contact, Email, SMS, Phone, Location, WhatsApp) with per-type forms (src/ui/contentForms.ts), debounced live preview via QRPreview class (src/core/encode.ts: qr-code-styling for QR, dedicated canvas for Aztec/DataMatrix), payload char counter, module-dimension status line ("33 × 33 modules"). Verified in xvfb GUI test: typing a URL updates the preview live.
cards.rejected: A generic single-textarea input (loses per-type validation and structure); per-type declarative field defs with validation were chosen instead.

cards.title: Styled dots & colors
cards.description: Dots shape (square/rounded/dots/classy), corner-square styles, foreground solid or linear/radial gradient, background color/transparent. Mapped straight onto qr-code-styling options.
cards.rationale: User-selected v1 feature; library shipped all of it, only wiring was needed.
cards.summary: Full qr-code-styling option surface wired through the StyleState store (src/core/store.ts) into src/ui/stylePanel.ts: dot shape, corner square/dot shapes, solid vs linear/radial gradient (angle, 2 color stops), background color + transparent toggle, quiet-zone margin, EC level L/M/Q/H. Persisted to localStorage (forge.style.v1).

cards.title: Logo / photo / emoji in the middle
cards.description: Two center-art sources sharing one pipeline: (a) image upload (file picker + drag&drop) with size/margin sliders and hide-background-dots toggle; (b) searchable emoji picker — render chosen emoji to an offscreen canvas via color-emoji font (Segoe UI Emoji on Windows, Noto Color Emoji — ships in the Freedesktop Flatpak runtime) → dataURL → same image path. When center art is present, force error-correction H; offer a white/rounded backing tile behind emoji (color glyphs need a quiet background to stay scannable); warn if art covers too many modules.
cards.rationale: User explicitly asked to add emoji alongside photo-in-the-middle. Reusing the same dataURL image pipeline makes emoji nearly free — the only new work is the picker UI and emoji→canvas rasterization. EC level H is required practice whenever the center is covered.
cards.summary: Center art shipped: image upload via file picker + drag & drop onto the preview (src/ui/stylePanel.ts importFileAsDataUrl), searchable emoji picker with 6 categories rasterized through the color-emoji font to a data URL (src/ui/emoji.ts), size/padding sliders, hide-dots-behind-art toggle, white rounded backing tile. Effective style forces EC level H whenever art is present (src/app.ts effectiveStyle).
cards.rejected: Rendering emoji as inline SVG text (color-emoji fonts render inconsistently in SVG); canvas rasterization to data URL chosen so emoji flows through the same image pipeline as uploaded logos.

cards.title: Export PNG / JPG / SVG + copy to clipboard
cards.description: SVG via qr-code-styling getRawData / own SVG serializer; PNG & JPEG via canvas.toBlob with quality slider; export resolution choice (256–2048 px). Save via IPC → main-process dialog.showSaveDialog → fs write (contextIsolation-clean, Flatpak-portal-friendly). Plus one-click Copy-to-clipboard (user-selected extra): rendered PNG → nativeImage through the IPC bridge to the system clipboard.
cards.rationale: Core requirement plus the user's chosen v1 extra. Clipboard copy goes through the same main-process bridge as save, so no renderer-side privileged APIs.
cards.rejected: Renderer-side fs/clipboard access (breaks contextIsolation and the sandbox model); all privileged work goes through the minimal IPC bridge (electron/main.ts export:save + clipboard:image).
cards.summary: Export shipped (src/ui/exporter.ts + src/app.ts doSave/doCopy): PNG/JPEG/SVG via renderExport, size 256–2048 px, JPEG quality slider; Save goes through IPC → main-process dialog.showSaveDialog → fs write; one-click Copy PNG → nativeImage → system clipboard.

cards.title: Extra barcode types: Aztec + DataMatrix (+ evaluate Micro QR)
cards.description: Use @zxing/library MultiFormatWriter to encode Aztec and DataMatrix into module matrices, then render them through the SAME styled canvas/SVG renderer used for QR so dot shapes, gradients and logo work on every type. Micro QR: evaluate — no mature JS encoder exists (ZXing lacks it); cut unless a solid lib appears.
cards.rationale: User wants parity with the original's symbologies (it did QR, Aztec, DataMatrix, Micro QR via zint/Pascal code). Sharing one styled renderer keeps the feature set uniform across types.
cards.rejected: Micro QR — cut: no mature JS encoder exists (ZXing has none); hand-rolling an encoder was not worth the correctness risk. A separate canvas path for Aztec/DataMatrix was rejected — one shared styled renderer keeps dot shapes/gradients/logo working on every kind.
cards.summary: Aztec + Data Matrix shipped (src/core/encode.ts): @zxing/library MultiFormatWriter encodes to a module matrix, rendered through the same styled canvas/SVG renderer (src/core/render2d.ts) so dot shapes, gradients and center art work on all three kinds. UI: QR/Aztec/DataMatrix segmented switch. Micro QR evaluated and cut.

cards.title: History / recent codes
cards.description: Store content + full options snapshot (styling, logo ref, type) in localStorage or electron-store; click to restore & regenerate; cap at ~20 entries; never store image blobs — regenerate from options.
cards.rationale: User-selected v1 feature. Snapshots are tiny (JSON) and regenerate deterministically, so history stays cheap and the list survives app restarts.
cards.summary: History shipped (src/ui/historyPanel.ts + store.addHistory/removeHistory/clearHistory): every save/copy pushes an entry (type, barcode, title, payload preview, content + full style snapshot), deduped, max 20, persisted to localStorage (forge.history.v1); one click restores content + style.
cards.rejected: Persisting history to disk via main process (needs new IPC + file management); localStorage keeps it sandboxed and zero-config, capped at 20 entries.

cards.title: Modern UI polish + dark/light theme
cards.description: CSS custom properties design system: cards, rounded corners, soft shadows, accent color, dark/light toggle persisted; single-window responsive layout (editor left, preview right, options panel).
cards.rationale: "Modernise the UI" is an explicit goal — the whole reason to not fork. A small token-based CSS system keeps the modern look consistent without a UI framework dependency.
cards.summary: Modern UI shipped: two-column layout (content forms left, preview/style/export/history right), CSS variables theme system with dark (default) + light toggle persisted per user (src/ui/theme.ts), custom tabs/segmented buttons/range inputs, i18n-ready string table (src/i18n/en.json, 128 keys) — all UI text flows through t().
cards.rejected: CSS framework (Tailwind) — hand-rolled CSS variables keep the bundle tiny and avoid a build dependency; a native menubar was dropped in favor of in-window controls with a chrome-less window on Windows/Linux.

cards.title: Windows packaging: NSIS installer + portable exe
cards.description: electron-builder targets: nsis (installer, per-user) + portable exe; app icon embedded; document that an unsigned exe triggers SmartScreen warnings — optional code signing later.
cards.rationale: User wants Windows packaging; NSIS+portable covers both install and USB-stick use with zero extra tooling beyond electron-builder.
cards.summary: Windows packaging shipped: npm run dist:win → NSIS installer (QR-Code-Forge-Setup-1.0.0.exe) + portable exe (QR-Code-Forge-Portable-1.0.0.exe) via electron-builder with rcedit under a fresh wine prefix + xvfb. Both artifacts verified in release/ and published to the GitHub v1.0.0 release.
cards.rejected: Code-signing the Windows binaries (no certificate available — binaries ship unsigned with a documented SmartScreen workaround); electron-updater auto-update (requires signed binaries to be trustworthy).

cards.title: Linux Flatpak packaging (io.github.<user>.qrcodeforge)
cards.description: flatpak-builder manifest: Freedesktop 24.08 runtime + org.electronjs.Electron2.BaseApp; npm ci && build renderer && electron-builder --dir, ship linux-unpacked. finish-args: --share=ipc, --socket=x11, --socket=wayland, --device=dri, --talk-name=org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop, --filesystem=home (for saves). Include .desktop, appstream metainfo (kept Flathub-ready), icons for io.github.<user>.qrcodeforge. Verify with flatpak-builder locally. DISTRIBUTION DECISION: GitHub Releases + locally-built Flatpak; no Flathub submission overhead.
cards.rationale: Flatpak is the user's preferred Linux format; the BaseApp approach is the Flathub-blessed Electron packaging method and works on any distro. User chose GitHub Releases distribution, so metainfo stays minimal but Flathub-compatible in case they change their mind.
cards.rejected: Flathub publication (decided with the user: GitHub Releases + local Flatpak for now); Tauri/AppImage-only fallbacks.
cards.summary: Flatpak shipped: manifest flatpak/io.github.lakisan1.qrcodeforge.yml (Freedesktop 24.08 runtime, Electron BaseApp, zypak sandboxing, npm ci with --share=network via manifest build-args), scripts/build-flatpak.sh (pins --default-branch=stable, --bundle emits a single-file .flatpak). Built, installed locally, bundle verified in release/flatpak/, published to the GitHub v1.0.0 release. Launch verified under Xvfb: zypak spawns the Electron binary inside the sandbox.

cards.title: Structured content types: WiFi, vCard, Email/SMS/phone, Geo, WhatsApp
cards.description: Tab switcher above the content editor. WiFi: SSID/password/encryption/hidden → standard WIFI: payload. vCard: name/phone/email/org → VCARD 3.0. Email/SMS/phone: mailto:/SMSTO:/tel: with subject/body. Geo: lat/lng fields → geo: URI. WhatsApp: phone + optional prefilled message → https://wa.me/<phone>?text=… (official click-to-chat URL; scanning opens the chat). Each type is a payload-string builder — styling, logo/emoji and export stay payload-agnostic.
cards.rationale: User selected every structured type plus WhatsApp when finalizing the plan. All of them reduce to small form UIs + serializer functions, so the real cost is form layout, not QR plumbing.
cards.rejected: Third-party form libraries; per-type hard-coded UI. Declarative field defs keep new content types a data-only change (schema lives in src/core/payload.ts CONTENT_TYPES).
cards.summary: Structured content types shipped (src/core/payload.ts + src/ui/contentForms.ts): Text/URL, WiFi (SSID/password/security/hidden), vCard contact, Email (to/subject/body), SMS, phone, geo location (lat/lng validated), WhatsApp (wa.me link with prefilled text). 12 unit tests cover the payload builders (tests/payload.test.ts).
